RM_2e23d41a-ed5c-5dd2-bedb-20e388002493: Kentucky bowhunter Ray Dunbar walks you through your first season with a bow: picking one, stringing it, and making that first clean shot.
RM_3e708c44-4b99-5e40-8e1c-c87561ae4f12: Howdy, folks. Ray Dunbar here, and today we're going bowhunting.

RM_a51fa50b-01c5-56dc-80d0-5e8d33ad2915: A good stave of hickory or ash, a sound string, and some patience. That's a bow.
RM_128baba8-01c8-5311-8750-e3c4dd948cd6: Always string it with your legs, not your arms. You'll thank me when your back doesn't go out.
RM_5de18836-5184-50e8-a61f-dbff975e7f9e: Stand sideways to the target. Feet about shoulder width. Like you're waiting for a bus.
RM_303febd3-f89c-5c57-8929-8125c0fecc71: Three fingers on the string: one above the arrow, two below. That's your Mediterranean draw.
RM_d82f0d7e-40a5-53b4-a554-82665aad98ab: Pull back to the same spot on your face every single time. Corner of the mouth works for me.
RM_da4db67f-7fbf-5053-b250-99640abd6130: That spot's called your anchor. No anchor, no accuracy. Simple as that.
RM_1d0037f8-562f-5470-9696-199c8210b0fa: Don't yank the string loose. Just relax your fingers and let the bow do the work.
RM_de32ae67-e268-5b0d-a541-caebcb4a8d71: See that? No bang, no echo. The deer two trees over didn't even look up.
RM_a06b47a4-1103-5a8c-b614-f690b43c63cf: That's the beauty of a bow, folks. Quiet as a church mouse.
RM_3af55764-e6d1-5d45-9b98-b80ab1249bb2: Go find your arrows after. Good arrows are worth walking for.
RM_17a5d2c7-165f-5247-bd79-01165f8600cf: I'm Ray Dunbar. Shoot straight, and I'll see you next time.
RM_4f4178ad-6338-5819-985e-f30ec44cc5da: VHS: Traditional Archery: Form and Release
RM_d5668edd-5cdf-5076-af30-cebdd0d12fe1: Coach Linda Pryor of the Louisville Archery Club breaks down the shot, from stance to follow-through, with slow-motion footage.
RM_c61e05ed-2ac8-5918-b515-245aeb2dfbb4: Welcome. I'm Linda Pryor, and this tape is about one thing: a repeatable shot.
RM_1d8ac2dd-5c90-5ca1-8cdd-ee4166a23347: Every good shot is the same shot. Same stance, same draw, same anchor, same release.
RM_79f4faeb-eda7-5ae2-824d-2936b370ab5d: Watch the bow arm here in slow motion. Locked, but not stiff. The elbow rolls out of the string's way.
RM_bded21b4-ddf5-5c06-af4e-68e6837156f5: Draw with your back, not your bicep. Squeeze those shoulder blades together.
RM_d2d894de-ae94-5144-b36e-1e5e4b2b414f: Beginners grip the bow like a hammer. Let it sit in the web of your hand instead.
RM_bef77899-cb28-512f-9c21-03168b1c2553: A tight grip torques the bow, and the arrow goes left. Every time.
RM_df71a872-fb3c-5ea8-9656-83d73006e343: Now the release. The string hand moves straight back, past your ear. That's your follow-through.
RM_b23aa2c3-9ac9-5d9d-9105-5d6eac61abdb: Hold your form until the arrow lands. Peeking early pulls the shot.
RM_a60de3ac-b570-53d0-9a3a-f2e572fc2bd9: If your arm is shaking at full draw, let down. A tired shot is a wasted arrow.
RM_a11e06de-fb3f-5efd-860a-fd4f9172c53e: [Slow-motion footage of an arrow flexing as it leaves the bow]
RM_19839b9f-e800-5842-acad-2f7b1534e0a3: Fifty arrows a day, every day, and you'll be surprised how fast it comes.
RM_0b36334f-37d0-52d9-abb4-fde08b45c591: Thanks for watching. Now go shoot.
RM_e0c9acbb-a64a-5720-bc6a-bbdcf74f46ac: VHS: The Silent Hunter: Advanced Bowhunting
RM_31a4e33d-e774-58e7-91c5-db5783b200e7: Ray Dunbar returns for the advanced course: shooting at range, moving targets, broadheads, and making every arrow count.
RM_863fd89e-30b9-58a4-9770-fbf57eda7be9: Ray Dunbar again. If you've watched the first tape, you're ready for the hard part.
RM_ecc4e436-7e07-5ef9-9667-376113535e13: Out past twenty yards, that arrow is dropping. Aim a touch high and learn your bow.
RM_8fa4fc3a-2637-503c-beaa-3d634d49caa4: Moving target? Lead it. Swing with the animal and release while you're still swinging.
RM_af26cf52-a5c8-50c7-a8ad-c40ead958944: Broadheads hit hard but they fly different. Practice with what you hunt with.
RM_2aa4042c-2c32-5c89-8855-1251eab6a5fb: Behind the shoulder, not the head. The big target is the sure target.
RM_dc081a76-97db-514e-922e-004c3e83d055: Wind in your face. Always. They can't hear you, but they sure can smell you.
RM_5d06a0dd-80dd-56b0-b46c-aabb23019bb1: Missed? Don't move. Nock another one, nice and slow. A quiet miss is a second chance.
RM_9be1e731-d2d9-50c7-9540-05eccc0d1174: A gun gets one shot before every critter in the county knows where you are. A bow gets as many as you've got arrows.
RM_bdd42d3c-371b-52a2-8e03-027aff399a1e: Check every arrow when you pick it up. A cracked shaft can come apart on the string.
RM_c1794482-d618-5a32-846a-48c54cd200ba: That's it for the advanced course. Stay patient, stay quiet, and you'll eat well.
